bull.b: The large recurring revenue base from instruments, accessories, and service ties growth to procedure volumes and the installed system base. This supports revenue visibility, customer retention, and durable cash generation as utilization expands across hospitals and surgical centers.

High operating margins and rapidly growing free cash flow give Intuitive substantial capacity to fund research, product development, customer support, and expansion internally. Strong cash conversion also improves resilience while allowing continued investment without relying heavily on debt.

Expansion of the installed base increases future opportunities for procedures, instruments, accessories, and service revenue. Double-digit procedure growth indicates continued adoption of robotic-assisted surgery and strengthens the network of clinical experience supporting further customer adoption.

bear.b: Slower growth reduces the pace at which Intuitive can expand its installed base and recurring procedure-related revenue. Although profitability remains strong, a moderating trajectory may make future earnings increasingly dependent on execution, new indications, and sustained adoption.

Weak Chinese tender activity and stronger domestic competition can constrain system placements and pricing in an important international market. The delayed clearance of da Vinci 5 in Mainland China may further limit product momentum and reduce the region’s contribution over the next several quarters.

Extended-use instruments could structurally lower recurring revenue earned per benign procedure, challenging the economics of the razor-and-blades model. At the same time, fewer bariatric cases and changing procedure mix may pressure instrument revenue even if total procedures continue growing.
